BL-1156.author: Claude (sprint 48, NR-962 ruled B, 2026-10-01)
BL-1156.title: A river divides its banks: the province fill pays to cross a course, not to travel along it
BL-1156.design: SETTLED (Ben, 2026-10-01, NR-962 B): PROVINCES.md, 'a river divides its banks'. Today the river bit sits on the step between a course tile and its downstream neighbour (river_generation.cpp ~223-230) and province.cpp ~212-213 charges +40 there, so the fill pays to travel along a river and crosses bank to bank free. BUILD: the fill pays the river cost to step onto or off a course across the flow (or an equivalent that makes the banks two sides); stepping along a course pays nothing extra. MEASURE FIRST, then after, on the 16 shipped seeds: the river:plain border ratio (1.19 on main), C13's per-seed river rows (red on 12, 37, 38), province counts and sizes. A row: river cost 0 must turn the river row red on the harness world AND the shipped seeds.

BL-1162.design: BEN'S NOTE (2026-10-03, keeping BL-1107's mapping for now): "I was considering amenities and goods that people consume through ages, rather than more commercial products." COMBINED RE-MEASURE (2026-10-05, drafts/sprint-49-household-remeasure.md): main + BL-1197 r3 + this stack, seeds 0/43/10, 400 ticks: 440 of 2,353 centres grew (seed 0 heads 79.5M -> 131.1M, seed 43 42.1M -> 71.9M, seed 10 52.8M -> 29.9M); fill/bid pooled: clean water 20%, medical 42%, consumer goods 18%, food rations 58%, water 77% (made in 3-6 of 14-25 bidding markets; 10-16k units shelved elsewhere), produce 86%. Gates 33.6/38.5/59.9 vs main 41.0/45.1/55.2. HELD until BL-1197 round 4 (derived demand: steel) lands and k is re-swept (NR-972) on the combined tree - with k = 0 a stocked shelf does not lower its market price, so the shipping gate cannot move shelved water to dry markets. Merging this stack needs world_save_version 34 (BL-1196 32 + BL-1201 33 collide) claimed in the ledger.

SUPERSEDED IN BUILD by BL-1196 (2026-10-05), which carries this branch and replaces its pro-rata fill with what households received. Merge the two together, held as BL-1196 says.

BUILT AND HELD UNMERGED (2026-10-04, 26cb6cbe on worktree-agent-a7a4ad16f983163e4; population_mvp ALL PASS 16): the per-market household gate reads the world correctly and the world fails it. centre_decline_trace, 400 play ticks: before, every centre declines from ~t180-260 (seed 0 heads 64.1M -> 76.7M -> 44.7M); after, every centre declines from the settle (seed 0 61.8M -> 32.4M -> 14.9M; seeds 10/41/43 alike), median met 0.10-0.11 at t400, never more than 70 centres at >= 0.50. Cause: water, clean water and medical supplies are supplied 0 on every seed (one exception, gone by t400), consumer goods fall to ~0 by t~100, food rations run 25-45% of demand. Those three zero goods carry 0.80 of the basket's 1.85 weight, so the best reachable ratio is 0.57 even with food and consumer goods met. The lane also defined the household fill as PRO-RATA (households get min(1, supply/demand) like every bidder; no new saved field) - a decision taken, alternatives being households first or last, each needing a saved per-market household record. HELD pending NR-967.

BASKET SETTLED (2026-10-04, on Ben's delegation; NR-967): the growth basket IS the household bid basket (POPULATION.md), met ratio = the share of the centre's own population bid its market filled, judged per market; population_growth.demand_basket retires; threshold 0.50. RULED (Ben, 2026-10-03): A+B -- the basket is household goods only (food, water, consumer goods), read against people's own demand, judged per market (POPULATION.md SETTLED). A short design pass settles the basket's contents first. Sprint 49. Unblocks BL-1139's abandonment.

FOUND 2026-10-03 (BL-1139 lane, centre_abandonment_census, 16 seeds, shipped start + 12 settle + 400 play ticks): with abandonment OFF, every centre on seed 0 (786) and seed 10 (879) is declining by tick 412 and villages fall to ~1k heads; on seed 0 none declines at tick 132, so the decline sets in between ticks 132 and 412. With abandonment ON all 4,544 scale-1 centres are deleted. Ben (2026-10-03): BL-1139's recorded ids merged; the abandonment itself (2f719556 on worktree-agent-ae9978d9141f0dc73) is HELD until this is diagnosed and fixed. WORK: trace the growth pass's decline inputs per centre over ticks 100-450 (labour demand, food, migration, habitability, wages, the play-side ceiling vs generation's carried capacity -- BL-1137's capacity_carried is generation scratch only and its note warns play-side demography must read it before clamping); name the cause; report for Ben before fixing.

BL-1185.author: Claude (the sprint 49 market viability sweep, 2026-10-04)

BL-1185.design:
MERGED to main (02da0166, 2026-10-05).

REACH CORRECTED (main session, 2026-10-05, superseding the REACH REFINED note below): the dispatcher's gate at BASE prices makes nothing reachable across markets when bases are equal - the dispatcher ships because the destination is SHORT. Generation-side: in reach iff the leg is viable AND reservation_mult x base_dst - haul > (1 + dispatch_margin) x base_src (each market's own base; ceiling off -> ceil_mult). Play-side (BL-1187's scorer): the literal dispatcher test on resolved prices. One helper, src/world/input_reach.

COLD REVIEW (2026-10-05, review/bl-1185 at 3bcff582): core rule sound; fix round sent - province cap bypass when the anchor is unplaced (HIGH), Pass 6 iteration burn, holdless corporations, the empty-budget roster path without a registry (Ben's ruling covers every pass), doc overclaims, charter_refusal_probe re-run. REACH REFINED (main session, 2026-10-05): the 0.95 x base haul bound was looser than the dispatcher's own export gate, so placement could call a lane in reach that never ships. One reach rule for placement and the scorer (BL-1187's input_reach helper): price_market_export_leg(...).viable AND dest_price - haul > (1 + dispatch_margin) x src_price, at each market's own base price in generation and its resolved price in play; with the ceiling OFF, reach does not collapse to same-market. Placement results with BL-1185 merged (5 seeds, 400 ticks, before the fixes): G1 18.6% -> 35.4%, G2 29.6% -> 26.5%, G3 32.2% -> 42.5%.

REACH DEFINED (2026-10-04, the BL-1186 diagnosis): a producer is within reach of a processor if (a) both tiles are in the same market, or (b) price_market_export_leg(producer market, consumer market).viable holds and the per-unit haul is at most (reservation_mult - 1 - dispatch_margin) x base (0.95 x base today). Placement CALLS the dispatcher's own function, so the two cannot disagree; when BL-1186's B1 lands, ported sea legs widen reach for both at once.

RULED (Ben, the sprint 49 form, 2026-10-04): pulled INTO sprint 49, and a HARD RULE, not a search score: no processor is placed without a producer of each of its inputs within reach. "Within reach" is the reach BL-1186 (goods cross markets) diagnoses, so BL-1186's diagnosis lands first.

The landscape search's winner hands play 119-141 input-starved processors of ~225 (seeds 0/43/37): whole chains (copper refining, alloys, machinery, electronics, spacecraft) have no input producer anywhere reachable, and coal is extracted in one market while steel mills stand in ten. BL-1193.author: Claude (the BL-1163 lane, 2026-10-04)
BL-1193.title: Households are a market nobody supplies: find why water, clean water and medical supplies never reach a market
BL-1193.design:
MERGED to main (915c6720, 2026-10-05).

DIAGNOSED (2026-10-04, a6eee332; docs/development/drafts/sprint-49-household-supply-diagnosis.md). (1) Household-good output is listed whole and bought by the market as buyer of last resort at the reference price with minted money (market_clearing.cpp:1418-1427); nothing ever takes it off the shelf, so shelves only grow (food rations 25-49k, consumer goods 1.8-3.5k, water ~8k by tick 200). (2) The household bid is a PRICING PULL ONLY (inject_population_demand adds to mc.demand, market_clearing.cpp:585); POPULATION.md:293 says a centre consumes its basket from the local market - the code is behind its doc. (3) A maker earns while it can run. (4) THE LOCK: households bid water nobody lists, the bid floors at 30% (elasticity_min), the shelf is not supply (k = 0), so water sits at 10x base from tick 2-3 everywhere, above the 2x ceiling, and clean-water/medical makers may not draw their own input; THE SWITCH: the strategic scorer moves clean-water plants (16 -> 0 by tick 3, seed 0) to consumer goods on base-price margin within "Welfare Goods" without checking inputs (corp_ai.cpp:1553-1630); THE CHURN: consumer-goods plants starve on food rations (over the ceiling in 19-22 of 24 markets) and steel, idle, then resume on a price-only estimate (building_profit.cpp:113ff). Food rations run but cover only 25-60% of the bid in 2-7 markets. (5) No water extractors on seeds 0 and 10: a firm opened for the water gap is placed on whatever its tile holds most (corporation_generation.cpp:476/548) yet counted against water's cap (:2667). FIXES FILED: BL-1196 (households consume from the shelf, H1+H4), BL-1197 (gap firm digs the gap resource, H5), BL-1187 widened (H6 + H7), NR-968 (H2).

Sprint 49, diagnosis first. On every seed water, clean water and medical supplies are supplied 0 at market across 400 play ticks, consumer goods fall to ~0 by tick ~100, and food rations run 25-45% of demand (the BL-1163 lane's centre_decline_trace, 2026-10-04). Yet steel_chain_probe sees 15 of 16 clean-water processors running at tick 0 on seed 0, so the output goes somewhere: name where (own pools, reservation, the shelf, a buyer of last resort, a household bid that is a pricing pull only and never fills). Then: is household demand a market a firm can PROFIT from (who pays, at what price)? If it is not, no placement or scorer change will make firms serve it. Read beside NR-968 (the price cycle) and BL-1185 (chain-feasible placement): household goods are the demand endpoints the chains exist for. Unblocks BL-1163 (NR-967).

BL-1194.author: Claude (the BL-1186 routing lane, 2026-10-04)
BL-1194.title: A sea leg costs less per distance than land on a highway, as ruled, so a long overseas haul beats a short overland one
BL-1194.design:
MERGED to main (53a1a740, 2026-10-05): sea 0.05 -> 0.002 per cost unit (0.005/tile, 0.0025 on a lane) vs a Highway plains tile 0.008; crossover with 0.10 handling per port: 67 tiles vs Highway, 40 vs Road, 24 vs Track, 13 vs unroaded (SUPPLY.md). Only exception: a highway through cities with the 50% node discount. Gates moved by divergence only (G2 seed 0 +20, seed 10 -25). sea_port_gate 49/0, supply_advance pass on main. Owed: haulage_measure's neighbour section still prices a whole crossing at the sea rate (BL-1165).

The ruling is already written (SUPPLY.md sec Logistical cost, Ben 2026-09-15): per distance, a sea leg costs less than land on a highway; every port charges handling per unit; the crossover distance is the design reading, reported whenever either term moves. The config inverts it: logistics.base_cost_per_unit_distance land 0.02, sea 0.05, and water tiles weigh 2.5, so a sea tile costs 0.125 against 0.02 for plains and sea never wins at any distance; BL-1186's port routes are taken only where no land path exists. WORK: retune so the ordering holds against a HIGHWAY tile (road multiplier included), measure and report the crossover distance with BL-1186's handling (0.10 per unit per port, a first cut), and re-derive anything priced off the haul (haulage_measure, the ceiling derivation - see BL-1165). Measure on BL-1184 (market viability gate).

BL-1196.author: Claude (the BL-1193 diagnosis, 2026-10-04)
BL-1196.title: A population centre consumes its basket off its market's shelf, as the doc says, and grows on what it received
BL-1196.design:
MERGED to main (90640c82, 2026-10-05) as the household stack: integration branch at k = 0 read G3 72.1% (seeds 0/43/10), heads 174M -> 289M, 718 centres grew; cold-reviewed, fix round; save v35; app build, save_load.lua (6 PASS), population_mvp 31/31, save_roundtrip OK on main. COMBINED RE-MEASURE (2026-10-05, drafts/sprint-49-household-remeasure.md): main + BL-1197 r3 + this stack, seeds 0/43/10, 400 ticks: 440 of 2,353 centres grew (seed 0 heads 79.5M -> 131.1M, seed 43 42.1M -> 71.9M, seed 10 52.8M -> 29.9M); fill/bid pooled: clean water 20%, medical 42%, consumer goods 18%, food rations 58%, water 77% (made in 3-6 of 14-25 bidding markets; 10-16k units shelved elsewhere), produce 86%. Gates 33.6/38.5/59.9 vs main 41.0/45.1/55.2. HELD until BL-1197 round 4 (derived demand: steel) lands and k is re-swept (NR-972) on the combined tree - with k = 0 a stocked shelf does not lower its market price, so the shipping gate cannot move shelved water to dry markets. Merging this stack needs world_save_version 34 (BL-1196 32 + BL-1201 33 collide) claimed in the ledger.

BUILT AND HELD (2026-10-05, 53e6b219 on worktree-agent-a4c46e4ea6977dcd0, on top of BL-1163's 26cb6cbe; population_mvp ALL PASS 27 incl. 60-tick drain rows; save v32, save_roundtrip OK; world_determinism PASS). Households draw their pooled bid off the shelf each clear (markets ascending, goods ascending), no money moves, and the growth gate reads fill / bid. Shelves now drain (seed 0 water 6.1k -> 0, food rations 5.4k -> 0). Centres still shrink on every seed by tick 400 (seed 0 heads 65.2M -> 19.5M; BL-1163 alone 14.9M) because water, clean water and medical supplies are never made (fill 0 of bid on seeds 0/10/43) and food rations fill only 20-30%: food + produce weigh 0.80 of 1.85, under the 0.5 threshold even when met. market_viability (0/43/10): G2 26.4% (main) -> 20.6%, the consumer-goods makers having lived off the uneaten food pile. HELD with BL-1163 until households are supplied (BL-1197, BL-1185, BL-1187). DECISION TAKEN by the lane, accepted: the household draw ignores the fair-price ceiling (that is a firm's reservation; a household's elastic bid already falls with price). SAVE: v31 is claimed by BL-1139 on an unmerged branch; whichever merges second rechecks. OPEN: this lane's "before" on main shows centres GROWING (met 1.000, 0 declining) while BL-1163's "before" showed them declining from ~t200 - the two instruments disagree on main; resolve before either merges.

DOC-MANDATED (POPULATION.md sec Population demand: "Each Tick, a population centre consumes a basket of goods drawn from the local market"; MARKETS.md sec Three properties: every resource needs a TERMINAL sink). Today the household bid only moves the price (market_clearing.cpp:585) and nothing leaves a shelf, so household-good shelves grow forever and the market's last-resort buy is the only buyer. BUILD: each clear, households draw their basket from the market's shelf (inventory), up to their bid, in a deterministic order; what they received is the household FILL (MARKETS.md sec Want and fill) and the growth gate reads it (BL-1163's met ratio = received / bid, replacing the pro-rata stand-in). Money: the market already paid the maker when it bought the stock, so consumption moves goods, not credits - state that in FINANCE.md's money loop if it is silent. A seam change (economy + save if a new record is persisted): Full mode, cold review, a multi-tick row (a one-tick row cannot see the shelf drain). Measure on BL-1184. Unblocks BL-1163 and removes NR-968's premise that inventory only grows.

BL-1197.author: Claude (the BL-1193 diagnosis, 2026-10-04)
BL-1197.title: A firm generated to fill a resource gap extracts that resource
BL-1197.design:
MERGED to main (a9823674, 2026-10-05): generation places Wells (Well > ice > nothing; the same firm takes the next good); the charter walk counts derived demand over goods the body can produce, closure by anchor route; unproducible unspent reason. market_viability seeds 0/43/10/28/38: G1 38.8 -> 54.6, G2 39.3 -> 47.7, G3 46.4 -> 63.0 vs main with BL-1201. Cold-reviewed, one fix round. Open: the density ceiling now binds (household goods 4-5 firms each) - asked of Ben.

RULED (Ben, 2026-10-05, the charter walk form): the walk counts DERIVED DEMAND - every standing or chartered processor's input demand (generation form, nominal rate) joins the gap the walk fills, recomputed as firms land; replaces round 3's raw-input special case (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md sec Pass 6). Round 3 (96328d42) measured: alloys/machinery back on 0/43, chain_infeasible 0 on 0/43/10, but steel - the input most chains lacked (consumer goods ~12,000 misses, machinery ~8,600) - was never chartered in its own right; gates 40.0/31.2/43.3 vs round 1 43.3/31.4/53.2.

BEN (2026-10-05, NR-973): "we can add wells to generation" - generation places Wells; the scorer keeps its K = 2 bucket.

REWORK SHAPE (main session, 2026-10-05, after BL-1198): a water-gap firm digs water at a WELL site (fresh-water adjacent) where its windows hold one, else falls back to the richest deposit and is not counted against water's cap; the three generation hooks BL-1198 named (author_building explicit target, the slot walk's is_well_site test, tile_score_for for a Well tile) carry it. The chain rule (BL-1185) then sees water near people and can place clean-water and medical makers.

FIRST BUILD DROPPED (2026-10-05, f2b3063d on worktree-agent-a1683c1bd7eda4279, not merged): placing every gap firm on the gap deposit, with no fallback, made every gate worse against BL-1185 alone (5 seeds, 400 ticks: G1 35.4% -> 20.3%, G2 26.5% -> 16.9%, G3 42.5% -> 27.5%; corps 111 -> 72 on seed 0) - a gap firm with no gap deposit in its windows placed nothing - and clean water still did not return on seeds 0/10/11/13/37. REWORK (main session, 2026-10-05): dig the gap good where the windows hold it, else fall back to the richest deposit AND do not count that firm against the gap good's cap (options c+b). OPEN QUESTION FIRST: seeds 10, 11, 13 and 37 have NO water extractor in any state, and seed 0 has 3 water mines yet no clean-water plant in reach. Measure water deposits per seed and per market on an earthlike body before reworking: if water deposits are near-absent, the household water chain is a deposit-generation question (TILES.md / RESOURCES.md), not a charter one.

GENERATION CHANGE (sprint 49 generation lane, after BL-1185). Seeds 0 and 10 have no water extractor at all; seed 43 has 2 in 1 of 18 markets. A firm opened to fill the water gap is placed on whatever its tile holds most of (corporation_generation.cpp:476, :548) yet still counted against water's per-resource cap (:2667), so the cap fills with firms digging something else. Place the gap firm on a tile of the gap resource, or do not count it. Measure water extractors per seed and BL-1184.

BL-1198.author: Claude (the sprint 49 main session, 2026-10-05)
BL-1198.title: Water can be drawn where people live on a habitable world, not only from ice
BL-1198.design:
MERGED to main (c39d2989, 2026-10-05).

BUILT, ROUND 2 OPEN (2026-10-05, a14a559f on worktree-agent-a26d22c169e545e60): placement_rules is_fresh_water_adjacent / is_well_site, a no-deposit Well yield (rate x 1.0, never exhausts), a scorer Well bucket (K=2 world-wide, ranked by habitability x water pull, placeable tiles only), construction ledger row, ACTIONS.json; well_gate P1-P8/E1-E2 PASS. Seed 43 G2/G3 fall (being attributed in round 2). GENERATION CANNOT PLACE A WELL: author_building (~454-487) takes its target from richest_extractable, the cluster slot walk (~620-630) tests can_place on the tile alone, tile_score_for (~402) scores a Well tile 0.001 - the BL-1197 rework places water-gap firms on Wells through these three hooks.

RULED (Ben, 2026-10-05, NR-971 A): the Well - an extraction_site targeting water, placement gated on fresh-water adjacency (a land tile a river runs through or bordering a lake), deposit-agnostic, mirroring the Fishing Wharf (placement_rules.cpp can_place / can_place_in_world, is_coastal). Spec in PRODUCTION.md sec Extraction buildings. Generation then has a water source near people: BL-1185's chain rule and BL-1197's gap firm can place wells; the scorer can build them. THEN re-sweep k (NR-972) and re-read the held household stack (BL-1163/1196/1179).

RESOURCES.md:147 seeds water deposits on ICY substrate only. On an earthlike home body that is the poles, so water - the household basket's heaviest unmet good, and the input of clean water and medical supplies - is almost never extracted near people: seeds 10/11/13/37 have no water extractor in any sprint 49 state, seed 0's three sit out of reach of any clean-water site, and household water fill is 5-24% (BL-1179 lane). No charter (BL-1197) or scorer (BL-1187) change can supply a good the ground does not hold where it is wanted. DESIGN CALL NR-971.

BL-1201.author: Claude (the BL-1198 lane diagnosis, 2026-10-05)
BL-1201.title: A standing sell order is a price floor over the whole surplus, with an optional cap, and closes itself when empty
BL-1201.design:
MERGED to main (7ab91754, 2026-10-05). Clean A/B on seeds 0/43/10, 400 ticks, vs main f37a12ea: G1 35.3% -> 41.0%, G2 30.6% -> 45.1%, G3 50.5% -> 55.2%; order-held units 0.0 in all 36 readings. agent_seam_harness 22/22 on main. OWED: a live click on the Market Ledger order form (Cap / qtr, 0 = no cap, rows read "all"); a visible auto-close notice (BL-1202).

RULED (Ben, 2026-10-05, in chat: options 3 + 1): a market rule for player and rivals alike, not an AI-only re-size - an order by default covers everything auto-surplus would list, at its floor; a quantity cap is optional; an order whose pool stands empty for a short run of ticks closes and the good returns to auto-surplus. Written into MARKETS.md step 4. The lane building the AI re-size was rescoped to this rule.

FOUND (2026-10-05, well_census --trace, seed 43): the scorer's trade candidate places ONE standing sell order per (corp, body, good), sized at half the excess over 50 units at that moment, no expiry (corp_ai.cpp:2120); it never re-sizes it and never issues remove_sell_order (corp_ai.cpp:2108-2118 refuses a second order). MARKETS.md step 4 exempts a resource under a standing order from auto-surplus ("the manual order governs", market_clearing.cpp:1163-1169, :1244-1245), and the order lists min(quantity, pool) per tick (:1305-1314). So production beyond the original quantity piles up for the rest of the campaign: water 18,168 order-held units by play tick 200, food rations 1,859, steel transiently 398; household demand reads unmet and prices sit at 8-9x. DECIDED (main session, 2026-10-05): fix on the AI side, not the market rule (the exemption is right for the player's own manual orders): when the pool under a rival's order outgrows the order (pool > k x quantity over several due ticks), the scorer re-sizes it via remove_sell_order + place_sell_order at the current surplus - existing verbs, inside the scored-trade grant (AI_OPPONENT.md sec 11). The player's orders are never touched. Measure on BL-1184 and well_census --trace (order-held units -> near 0).

BL-1202.author: Claude (the BL-1201 fix round, 2026-10-05)
BL-1202.title: The player sees when one of their standing sell orders closes itself

BL-1203.author: Claude (the k re-sweep, 2026-10-05)
BL-1203.title: Surplus water reaches the markets that are dry
BL-1203.design:

Room = dispatch_absorbable on dm.demand (the want register): households bid at the posted ~7x price so their elastic bid has collapsed, and processors' water want is absent - a draw over 2x does not bid (BL-1172). Counterfactual room per dry market: today 1.15; households re-read at the landed price 7.64; plus the suppressed processor want 11.51. Also: each shelf exports to one destination per pass (supply_system.cpp:1310). The same mechanism stalls construction on steel (BL-1183). ROOM RULING ASKED OF BEN.

Found by the k re-sweep (2026-10-05, drafts/sprint-49-k-resweep.md, integration branch): 2.5-6k units of water sit on surplus shelves while 15-18 consuming markets are dry, and water shipped between markets stays 8-22 units/tick at every k. k > 0 drops stocked markets' price to 1.4-1.5x and cuts seed 0's price-gate refusals from 75 to 13 per tick, but two other brakes remain: (1) NO ROUTE - most refusals are "no port reached overland" (seed 0's 2,066-unit shelf at 0.59x reaches no market); (2) NO ROOM - a dry market's household demand has collapsed at the price ceiling (0.1-1.4 units), so a shipment has little to fill. BL-1206.author: Claude (sprint 49 close-out, 2026-10-06)
BL-1206.title: The seated corporation operates at a profit from day 1 on every curated seed

BL-1278.design: DIRECTION RULED (Ben, 2026-10-10, option C; always hit): NATION_GENERATION.md § The nation count is a target. Total <= 40, major 1..6, total >= major. Stage 1, the lean: the total sets placement seed density; the major target leans charter-capital concentration. Stage 2, reconciliation by history verbs: conquest/absorption (too many nations), a subject freed or a province seceding (too few), a national champion chartered in the richest championless minor (too few majors), a cross-border buy-out (too many majors). OPEN before build: which span runs reconciliation; how the richest minor is read; buy-out pricing; how the merge pass's min-territory stop composes with a target. MEASURE FIRST: the natural total and major counts across the 16 library seeds (living polities run ~40-115, so the 40 cap reconciles on nearly every seed). Gate: every library seed lands on both targets across a grid of target pairs, each correction recorded as a history event. RULED (Ben, 2026-10-11): reconciliation runs in the closing rounds of Industrialisation, before the polity fold (NATION_GENERATION.md). Still open: richest-minor reading, buy-out pricing, the min-territory stop. RULED (Ben, 2026-10-11): richest minor = most industry points on its ground; buy-out = the richest champion buys the poorest major's specialist whole at its charter price; the min-territory floor runs first and reconciliation closes the remaining gap (NATION_GENERATION.md § The nation count is a target). No open calls remain. BUILD CALLS (Ben, 2026-10-11, on the build plan): the size floor moves into the history as closing-round absorptions; the total is reconciled in Industrialisation's closing rounds; the majors are reconciled after the landscape search with events dated back; a minor that cannot afford its champion gets a state charter (treasury makes up the gap); unset targets keep the natural count, uncapped; the total's lean acts on conquest appetite and secession pressure. BL-1286.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the history-patterns form); filed by Claude
BL-1286.title: Detectors for the five history patterns, measured across the 16 library seeds before any target is built
BL-1286.design: DESIGNED (Ben, 2026-10-10): GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § History patterns. One predicate per pattern over the history record (lapse_event + span records), naming the polities it touched; emits pattern tags carried polity -> nation (NATION_GENERATION's fold). FIRST: measure how often each pattern already happens across the 16 library seeds, unforced - it sets each lean's size and whether reconciliation has much to do. The detectors are also the gates of BL-1287, BL-1288, BL-1289. MEASURED (2026-10-11, tools/verify/history_patterns.cpp over the 16 library seeds, provisional thresholds, main 54d462a0): rise and fall 0/16 (largest realm peaks at 7.6-22.6% of held regions, none near the 50% hegemony cap; 9/16 peak in the second half of Empires; none halves with a successor breaking from it); late culture 0/16 (the most isolated founding culture has no living realm at the Empires close on 8/16 seeds and is never bound in Exploration; Exploration binds 0-5 of 28-75 cultures); world war 0/16 (at most 3 of the six most populous realms touched by conflict in any 30-year window; total population never falls in the span); civil war 16/16 under the loose reading (a successor with a quarter of its parent fights it within 50 years: 4-175 per seed - the existing secession already makes it, minus the civilian famine/displacement mechanism); revolution 0/16 (the Industrialisation span records no split at all). BL-1278 reading: nations 20-69 (9/16 over 40), living polities 37-95, nations with a planned specialist 3-11 (3/16 over 6). The src/ detectors and tags remain this item's build. RULED (Ben, 2026-10-11): the detectors take the readings written into CIVILISATION.md (rise size floor, civil war reading) and EXPLORATION.md (late culture at the Culture close). src HALF BUILT AND MERGED (757cbad4): src/world/history_pattern_detectors.*, tags folded onto the report with dead realms passing theirs on; full tier: rise and fall 0/16, late culture 1/16, world war 0/16, civil war 16/16, revolution 0/16 (the targets are BL-1287/1288/1289). Follow-up: one source for the civil-war thresholds shared by sim and detector.

RULED (Ben, 2026-10-12): the realm largest at 200 BCE rises; peaks by 400 CE; its share halves within 300 years of the peak; backstop = the lean escalates in bounded recorded steps until the detector passes (CIVILISATION.md).

RULED (Ben, 2026-10-11): the lag is development diffusing by contact in proportion to reach; every culture feels it, the most remote receives least (EXPLORATION.md). BL-1340.author: Ben (2026-10-16 playtest); filed by Claude
BL-1340.title: A road is an edge between two tiles, not a property of one
BL-1340.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16 playtest): 'Roads should be directional, so they always cross the edge of two tiles.' RULED (Ben, 2026-10-16): roads move to EDGES, as rivers already are - not a rendering-only change. DESIGNED: LOGISTICS.md section 4 (Roads - an edge between two tiles) and RENDERING.md (Roads draw across the edge they cross). Grain: a tier per hex side, six sides, two bits each (0 none / 1 Track / 2 Road / 3 Highway), both tiles of an edge carrying it as both tiles of a river crossing do, side i mirroring side i+3. The road multiplier moves from the node to the EDGE in logistics.cpp edge_cost, beside the river discount that already lives there (A* keeps its 4-cardinal walk and its hex_side_for_offset derivation). Every count of roaded TILES becomes a count of roaded EDGES, each edge once: Logistic Points, network upkeep, reach, interdiction. Placement names a tile AND a side. Pre-v53 saves migrate by laying, between each pair of 4-cardinal neighbours that both carried a road, an edge at the LOWER of their two tiers. World save v53 claimed. A WORLD-MOVER: measure haulage_measure --far-trade and market_viability before and after; a re-bless is Ben's. BRIDGES GRANTED (Ben, 2026-10-17): "edge means from one tile centre to another, but not only one tile centre. This should allow spanning water with bridges" / "Roads can go over water with bridges no problem." So a road edge is permitted where EITHER END is water, and a run of such edges across a strait IS a bridge - no second mechanism, no new field. A bridge edge prices as its tier, and a crossing made on one is paid at that road price rather than the water sea-leg price. What stays forbidden is only the original target: a road that is a property of ONE tile. This unblocks the four road_generation_harness rows the build left red (R6a markets off the backbone, R6b/R6d trunk links stamping nothing, R2s-a) and the 15 markets stranded off their nation backbone. HAULAGE ACCEPTED (Ben, 2026-10-17): the far-trade drop (pooled window Y units -28%, share past the nearest market +2-5 points) is the intended meaning - a road discounts only the crossing it covers - so no re-tune; re-measure after bridges land, since they change it again. COLD REVIEW 2026-10-17: do-not-merge, eight findings, fix round sent. Save seam, mirror invariant across every writer, count_road_edges sides-0-2 and the wire seam all judged correct and unbreakable. The eight: place_road side inserted before tier so five 5-arg calls read tier as side (logistics_harness T10 and building_upkeep R11f red, neither run); stamp_edge returns true having laid nothing, which is the mechanism behind the 15 off-backbone markets and needs no design call; two of six sides can never be crossed by a 4-cardinal walk yet auto_road_side and the street loop offer them, so a road can be bought, counted and billed while crossing nothing - RULED in LOGISTICS.md section 4 (Only a side a walk can cross may carry a road), the field stays six-wide and the restriction is on what may be written; body_reach_field lost the road discount entirely so roads no longer shorten reach and corp_ai scores a road that buys nothing; lane_clock hop_cost lost it too so a convoy clock drifts against its own priced path; network_upkeep bills nothing where the canonical half is unowned land, about half of frontier roads by grid orientation, and count_road_edges has no production caller so the verified function is not the one that runs; a UI neighbour-signature bit collision hides a sea lane when survey flips; corp_ai can now buy 18 edges on one tile instead of 3. Also noted: every pre-v53 save loses its isolated village streets on load, which is the ruled migration, so it stands - the lane is reporting how many tiles it drops. R6a CLOSED 2026-10-17 by diagnosis, not by weakening: market 47845 sat on land carrying no road, its nation held 11 towns and 85 roaded cells, and the join pass tried once and found no joined cell. The PASS was right and the ROW asked the weaker question - it wanted a route to a TOWN, where the join needs a route to the nation ROAD NETWORK (roaded and reachable from its towns). A town is not a network. The row now rebuilds that network from the towns outward with its own walker and names the exemption for the reason the pass applies; written into LOGISTICS.md as the third case beside no-town and no-route. road_generation_harness went 8 red at the first cut, then 4, then 1, then ZERO. ALL GATES GREEN: market_viability FULL 16/16 shards with no failing row (pooled G1 92.2 / G1t50 88.6 / G1b 3.0 / G2 182.3 / G3 96.2, and seed 38 pre-bridge failures gone), player_seed_sweep 12/12, world_determinism, save_roundtrip, logistics_harness, building_upkeep, logistics_reach_harness, nation_tech, tax_discontent, space_assets all pass, history_sim at its R3a2/R3a3 baseline. HAULAGE RECOVERED: pooled window Y units sold at destination 2221.7 (main) -> 1606.0 (pre-bridge, -28%) -> 2283.2 (post-bridge), on a third fewer convoys carrying 11% more volume with a higher share going past the nearest market - but NOT uniform, seeds 9 and 11 down against main, 10 and 12 well up, so read per seed. A bridge hop prices as its deck (Track bridge 0.667 against a bare water hop 1.750). Village streets the v52 migration drops: single digits a world (9 street-only centres of 176 on seed 0), each one a lone street that joined nothing even then. DELIVERED 2026-10-17 (live click: Ben, 'The roads draw right now'). road_level (uint8 per tile) became road_edges (uint16, two bits a side, six sides, odd-r order), both tiles of a crossing carrying it with the mirror asserted; the discount moved from the node to the crossing and then into ONE shared edge_traversal_cost that all six readers call (A*, the flood field, the port hop, body_reach_field's Dijkstra, lane_clock's hop_cost, the march) - a better fix than the per-reader patches the review asked for, and one that cannot drift again. World save v53 with a migration (between 4-cardinal neighbours that both carried a road, an edge at the lower tier), refusing the whole stream on a mirror violation. Bridges granted the same day: a crossing may have a water end, a run of them is a bridge priced as its deck, and the player's must touch land at one end. Only a side a 4-cardinal walk can cross may carry a road. GATES, all green on merged main: road_edges 38/0, road_generation_harness ROAD GEN AUDIT OK (from 8 red rows, through 4 and 1, to 0), world_determinism, save_roundtrip, logistics_harness, building_upkeep, logistics_reach_harness, nation_tech, tax_discontent, space_assets, market_viability FULL 16/16 shards with no failing row (and seed 38's pre-existing failures gone), player_seed_sweep 12/12, history_sim at its R3a2/R3a3 baseline. HAULAGE: pooled far-sold volume 2221.7 (main) -> 1606.0 (pre-bridge) -> 2283.2, on a third fewer convoys carrying 11% more, per-seed mixed. Tail: BL-1348, BL-1357 (the doc's lay-from-a-road and border rules are not yet in code), BL-1369, BL-1372.

BL-1346.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the market attraction form); filed by Claude
BL-1346.title: A tile clears at the market it is most attracted to: logistics cost over the centre's pull, not grid distance
BL-1346.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): "Markets should be mildly dynamic, where each tile has a market attraction for each market, based on logistics distance to that market centre and also a modifier for that market centre which can come from either tech nodes or buildings." DESIGNED: MARKETS.md section Catchment is an attraction, not a distance; LOGISTICS.md section 3b (the off-road leg); GLOSSARY Market attraction. Today market_for_tile is nearest centre_tile by SQUARED GRID DISTANCE, column wrapped (market_clearing.cpp:165-284), cached in an unsaved raster rebuilt on market-set change - it cannot see a road, a tech or a building. New: attraction = traversal cost (LOGISTICS.md section 1) / centre pull, lowest wins, ties to the lowest market id; pull is a modifier_set multiplier, 1 by default. OFF-ROAD (Ben's call): a tile with no roaded edge costs the nearest roaded tile's network cost PLUS off-road-per-tile x the 4-cardinal step count to it (column wrapped), so every tile belongs to a market and far land drifts between markets as roads approach. Reach (section 3) is NOT changed - catchment and permission stay separate. CADENCE (Ben's call): recompute on change - a road laid or cut, a pull gained or lost, a market carved or folded - never on a clock, so it stays a pure function of standing state and is still never saved. A WORLD-MOVER: measure market_viability and haulage_measure --far-trade before and after; a re-bless is Ben's. Sequenced after BL-1340 (roads are edges), which changes what a roaded tile is. SAME-NATION BONUS (Ben, 2026-10-16): a tile owned by the same nation as the centre is 1.2x as attracted to it - a property of the (tile, centre) PAIR, not of the centre, so a centre pulls harder only on its own ground. Written into MARKETS.md. Measure how many tiles actually change hands at 1.2: the bonus is small against the cost spread, so report the count of tiles whose market flips because of it, per seed, and say so if it flips almost none. DELIVERED 2026-10-19. The field is one Dijkstra per centre over the body - a roaded edge priced by edge_traversal_cost (read_river false, as the reach field does), anything else by the off-road leg times the ground it crosses - divided by the centre's pull and by the same-nation 1.2x on the PAIR, lowest wins, ties to the lowest market id, folds mapped to their absorber. Cached in the existing per-body raster behind a new world::catchment_generation stamp, bumped by the road writer and by world::set_tile_nation; nothing is serialised. A COLD REVIEW FOUND TWO HIGH DEFECTS in the first cut and both were fixed before landing: a centre-independent off-road anchor that could discard a reachable network (laying a disconnected crossing made a tile's cost jump, i.e. the field was not monotone in roads), and a cadence folded off invalidate_logistics_caches, which fires inside per-building loops that read market_for_tile - a rebuild per idling port, each a Dijkstra per centre. THE CENSUS BEN ASKED FOR: the 1.2x moves 279 of 31581 tiles on seed 0, 0.88%. Gates: market_attraction_harness 16/0, world_determinism, save_roundtrip, logistics_harness, market_fold_fixture green; market_viability FULL pooled G1 92.0 -> 90.1, G2 182.1 -> 185.0, all five gates pass on both sides. THE TRADE MEASUREMENT, now taken: haulage_measure --far-trade, 4 seeds from 0, on the commit before (7f4f9461) and after: window E 771 convoys / 3543.5 units -> 1112 / 6282.9, window Y 841 / 4188.6 -> 1159 / 6733.7. That is +44% and +77% of traffic in the early window and +38% / +61% in the year window, with the volume SOLD at its destination up too (1430.9 -> 1457.6 and 1250.9 -> 1602.2). The direction is the item working: a tile now clears at the market its goods can actually reach along a road, so more pairs of markets are worth hauling between. It is a LARGE move and Ben should see it, because convoy traffic is the quantity no golden can see. OWED: a pull fixture once BL-1350 gives pull something to read.

DESIGNED: PRODUCTION.md section A building needs a road; LOGISTICS.md section 4 (Generation roads every building site). A tile carries a road when any of its hex sides carries a roaded edge - a crossing INTO the tile is a road ON it, from either side. EXTRACTION IS NOT EXEMPT (Ben's call): a remote deposit is worked only once a road reaches it, which with BL-1348 means a chain of crossings built out to it one tile at a time - the intended cost of far ore. GENERATION IS BOUND TOO (Ben's call): the road pass lays a crossing to every site it stamps, so the 1960 world holds no building the rule would refuse; exempting generated buildings would make the opening world the one place the rule fails. Add the refusal to placement_rules.cpp beside the stack and ceiling checks, with a message that names the road. BL-1351.author: Ben (2026-10-16: "we can take a look at generation to make sure logistics producing assets give points across each nation"); filed by Claude
BL-1351.title: Verify that generation's seeded logistics sources really cover every nation
BL-1351.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16: "we can take a look at generation to make sure logistics producing assets give points across each nation"). CORRECTION, 2026-10-16: an earlier revision of this item claimed a landlocked nation has NO Logistic Points because corporation_generation's building mixes seed ports but no inland hub. The mixes do lack the hub (corporation_generation.cpp:305, the hub appears only as a placement score at :449) - but a DEDICATED pass seeds them: seed_logistics_sources (logistic_points.cpp:382) places inland_logistics_hubs at world fold until every consumer on a nation's ground has coverage 1 and every pool meets claim x k_pool_margin (2.0), bounded by k_max_hubs 4000 over 64 sufficiency rounds, siting a hub on the serving market's centre_tile where that is on the nation's dry ground and on the consumer's own tile otherwise. So coverage is engineered by construction, and this item is MEASUREMENT, not new work. THE WORK: measure per nation on the curated seeds - sources seeded by network, tiles covered, pool made against claim, and how many nations fall back to on-consumer-tile hubs rather than market centres. That also tests Ben's picture (a centralised capital with high points, diminishing with distance, extended by outlying hubs): if hubs land mostly on consumer tiles rather than at centres, the picture will not appear however the lens is drawn. DELIVERED 2026-10-17: tools/verify/lp_coverage_census.cpp merged, 16 curated seeds in 168-196 s, deterministic twice over, cross-checked against lp_pool_harness seed 0 line for line. THE BASELINE: 707 hubs over 16 worlds (44.2 a world, 1.1% of k_max_hubs 4000); seeding costs 59 ms mean at the fold; 0 pre-existing hubs, so every road source is this pass; 5,544 consumers ALL at coverage 1, none partial, none uncovered; no nation anywhere short of its claim; pooled margin 8.47 against k_pool_margin 2.0, so pass 2 is nearly idle. AND THE THREE FINDINGS: only 10.3% of hubs land on a market centre_tile (73 of 707), structurally capped because the dedupe allows one hub a centre and the reach test from a bare centre rejects most; points barely fade from the capital (83/73/65/39 per tile by distance ring, the capital the peak of its own field in 19% of cases and holding ZERO points in 28%); and coverage is building-local, not territorial - 98.7% of building tiles and 100% of consumers covered against 78.1% of national ground at coverage 0, so a lens reading the field as a map will look like confetti. 48% of nation-rows (347 of 730, every one a minor) hold ground and get no pool - harmless today because those are exactly the nations with no consumer on their ground, latent the moment anything is built there. Landlocked nations are weakest on every axis. Re-run form is key=value records by prefix so two runs diff as numbers; re-run unchanged after roads-as-edges, the road-tier reach extension and rail point-to-point. Successor: BL-1367.

BL-1354.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the logistics visibility message); filed by Claude
BL-1354.title: Tile selection gains a Logistics section: the points provided here and the points consumed here
BL-1354.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): "we should improve visibility by giving tile selection a surface for logistics. We should show the number of logistics points provided, and the number consumed by that tile." Attach in COLUMN 3, the Tile card, right after the 'Tile [x, y] - <road tier>' title row and before the building grid (selection_panel.cpp:2999-3001) - already the tile-grain, road-aware spot, and a BeginChild that scrolls on its own. A fifth column would break SELECTION.md's four-column ruling (Ben, 2026-10-13); the disabled Supply action button is the cheaper alternative if the card proves too tight. EVERY FIGURE IS ALREADY IN SCOPE at that draw site: the economy_report gives report.logistic_points - per building need / coverage / granted / class, and per nation pool / made[3] / sources[3] / claim[3] / granted[3] / rule_set - and w is non-const there, so lp_coverage_at(w, memo, tile_id) gives the coverage a building on this tile WOULD get even with nothing built, which is the one genuinely per-tile figure. BL-1356.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the Logistic Points form); filed by Claude
BL-1356.title: A tile requests the points it needs and they are routed to it over one path, split across sources in distance order
BL-1356.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16, on the LP form: "Both: surfaces now, routing straight after"). DESIGNED: LOGISTICS.md section How a tile's points get to it. SEQUENCE IS BEN'S: BL-1352 (one system), BL-1353 (lens) and BL-1354 (tile surface) land FIRST, so routing is measured against honest numbers rather than guessed - the real model's reach already fades with distance and extends with outlying hubs, and nobody has yet seen it drawn. THE MODEL: today there is no routing at all - a nation-wide scalar pool scaled by a per-tile reach field (max over the nation's three networks), granted pro-rata or by the share rule. New: a tile's request is the sum of its buildings' needs; it is filled over ONE best path, never two at once; a source fills part of a request only if it both reaches the tile AND is itself connected back toward the market centre (Ben: "further sources have to both reach the tile, and produce enough to extend backward towards the market centre"), so points arrive along a chain the centre anchors and an isolated hub supplies nothing; where the nearest source falls short the remainder comes from the next nearest that satisfies both tests, in distance order. This supersedes the older constraint-2 rule that a draw lands on exactly one anchor. SCARCITY (Ben's ruling): distance ORDERS the queue and never raises the bill - requests inside the falloff range are served first, then those beyond, and a far building draws the same points as a near one. The settled rule 'the draw is what moves, not how far' therefore stands; NR-620 measured a 73% convoy-traffic collapse the one time a distance draw was tried, so any implementation that makes a far building cost more points is wrong by ruling, not by taste. MARCHES (Ben's ruling): a march draws the nation pool and competes with production. RULED (Ben, 2026-10-16): the march CLAIMS FIRST, keeping his 2026-09-24 ruling (NR-917) literally now that its other half is gone - it arbitrated armies against trade, and trade draws nothing, so a march is supplied before the production behind it. Written into LOGISTICS.md. Determinism: allocation must stay order-independent - a deterministic priority over a sorted set, never first-come by iteration order (the march draw is first-come in unit-id order today, economy_system.cpp:4210). A WORLD-MOVER: measure market_viability, haulage_measure --far-trade and per-nation output before and after. DELIVERED 2026-10-21 on Ben's rulings, all in LOGISTICS.md: (1) the routing form 2026-10-20 - one nation pool, the fade caps a source's share and the next tops it up, after the march production then trade, no-rule classes one queue; (2) the anchor: direct reach measured G1 96.0 -> 71.2 and was replaced by a CHAIN, and a chain to the market centre stranded consumers in foreign-centred markets, so the chain anchors at the nation's CAPITAL (2026-10-21); (3) only connected sources feed the pool (NR-1057), a link counts either way (NR-1058), and rival chain-laying is granted as BL-1395 (NR-1059). Generation lays hubs outward along the chain (steered over the nation's own ground) and bridges ground cut off by water with port pairs measured over water only, island-hopping across two passes. Three cold reviews; every finding fixed or raised. MEASURED, before (BL-1360 landed) -> after: market_viability FULL pooled G1 96.0 -> 94.7, G1t50 89.1 -> 86.8, G1b 2.5 -> 2.3, G2 173.3 -> 170.5, G3 97.1 -> 94.9, all passing; per seed G1t50 under 85 on 46 (84.4), 28 (77.1, the island seed), 40 (83.4), 41 (84.8). haulage_measure --far-trade window E 549 -> 900 convoys (5143.8 -> 7554.4 u), window Y 577 -> 959 (6378.8 -> 5920.6 u). lp_coverage_census seeds 0/28/46: every consumer covered (360/324/321), 216 hubs and 17 ports (9 islands bridged), seeding ~50 ms a seed. logistic_points_harness 80/0; lp_pool_harness M/L1/L2/L5 pass on an independent chain (L7 is BL-1383's old red row); world_determinism ALL PASS; save_roundtrip OK.

BL-1357.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the Logistic Points form); filed by Claude
BL-1357.title: A road may always be built across a national border, and never further
BL-1357.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): "if another nation holds the market centre, we may not be able to even build roads to supply LP. So due to this case, it should always be possible to build a road over a national border, but not further." DESIGNED: LOGISTICS.md section 4 (A road may always cross a national border). From a tile you hold, one crossing into a neighbour's tile is always permitted; that foreign tile is not then a tile you may build FROM, so the road stops where it lands - a connection, never a corridor. It is the exception that keeps BL-1348 (a road is laid from a road) from making a foreign-held market centre unreachable, which under BL-1356 would make every tile behind it unsuppliable. Sequenced after BL-1340 and BL-1348, whose placement rule it amends.DELIVERED 2026-10-18. The same gate compares the named tile's tile_to_nation holder against the acting corporation's home nation (reason foreign_ground): nothing refuses the crossing INTO foreign ground, but the tile it lands on is not one that actor may build FROM - a connection, never a corridor. can_place_road and road_crossing_targets gained an actor parameter, null_entity meaning nation-blind for generation and the affordance read, and verify.road_admits takes it too so the oracle and the highlight cannot disagree at a border. It is the exception that stops BL-1348 making a foreign-held market centre unreachable, which under the routed Logistic Point rules would strand every tile behind it. The cap was retired in BL-1309's cut and the code still stands, zeroed: market_lp_left (supply_system.cpp:1035) returns 0.0f, commit_trade_shipment (:1083) voids the pools and the refusal, market_component::trade_lp_spare is permanently 0 yet serialised at save v46 and still read by corp_ai's rival-Marketplace estimate, and corp_command::rejected_no_lp serves a gate that draws nothing. THE DRAW: cargo quantity at the anchor the shipment leaves - the settled formula, what moves and not how far, so it does not reintroduce the distance draw NR-620 measured at a 73% convoy-traffic collapse. BL-1367.author: Claude (from the BL-1351 census, 2026-10-17)

BL-1367.design: SPRINT 55 (from the BL-1351 census, 2026-10-17). Ben, 2026-10-16: 'What we want to see is a centralised market capital city, with a high number of logistics points, and logistics diminishing as we get further away, but extended by logistics buildings further away.' Excluded nations and market anchors by cover (A line) are printed. BL-1375.author: Ben (2026-10-17: "not every road is rendering"); diagnosed and filed by Claude
BL-1375.title: A crossing with a water end never draws: the bake still skips road data on water tiles
BL-1375.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-17, at the live click: 'The logic seems to work, but not every road is rendering'). DIAGNOSED BY READING: ground_bake.cpp:748 gates the road copy on 'if (!water && tile_has_road(t))', so a WATER tile never gets s.road[i] or s.road_sides[i] filled at all - that guard predates bridges and Ben's 2026-10-17 bridge ruling invalidated it. Two consequences, both matching what he sees: a bridge deck over water draws nothing, AND the LAND side of a shore crossing draws nothing either, because route_paint.cpp road_links_of (:130) gates every neighbour on on_net(s.road, nc, nr) (:139) and the water neighbour reads as not-on-net, so no link bit is set and no stroke is drawn. Inland roads are unaffected, which is why it reads as 'not EVERY road'. Row parity is NOT the cause - road_links_of already derives the side per parity via hex_side_for_offset. THE WORK: fill s.road / s.road_sides for a water tile that carries a road edge (the deck), let on_net and road_links_of see it, and paint the deck in route_paint, which today has only a sea-lane wake on water. Check the bake_source tile_class water branch does not skip route painting as well. RENDERING.md already rules a road draws as a run crossing the boundary it crosses, so the doc is right and the code is behind it. Verify with a capture of a bridge at a strait and of a shore crossing, and extend scripts/verify/roads.lua to assert a bridged crossing publishes a link bit. DELIVERED 2026-10-17 (live click: Ben, 'The roads draw right now'). The bake's road copy was gated on !water, a guard that predated bridges, so a water tile got no road data and neither the deck NOR the land side of a shore crossing drew (route_paint's road_links_of gates each neighbour on on_net, and the water neighbour read as empty). Both fixed; the deck is the run carried over the water - same tier width, colour and crossing points, no verge, embankment or water tint, one narrow shadow, no ornament - now written into RENDERING.md. THE CHECK WAS PROVED TO FAIL ON THE OLD CODE: restoring the guard gave exactly 200 crossings drawn at neither end (160 shore + 40 span) and 0 water tiles with road data, which is Ben's complaint measured. BL-1376.author: Claude (found delivering BL-1375, 2026-10-17)
BL-1376.title: Generation lays 105 crossings from land onto a water tile with no continuation, and they now draw as jetties
BL-1376.design: SPRINT 55 (found delivering BL-1375, 2026-10-17). Now that a crossing with a water end DRAWS, the data shows what it always held: of 170 water tiles carrying road data on the measured seed, 105 carry only ONE link - a crossing laid from land onto a water tile that continues nowhere. They render as a half-hex jetty into the sea. The renderer is faithful: hiding them would recreate the original defect in a new form, a crossing bought, billed and drawn by nothing, and roads.lua prints the count every run. THE QUESTION IS UPSTREAM: why does road generation lay a crossing onto a water tile with no continuation? Either it is a bridge whose far half the pass failed to lay (then the pass is wrong and should lay both or neither - note it already counts a link as laid only if a crossing was written, so this is a different hole), or a deliberate quay/landing (then it wants a name and a look, not an accident of the road field). BEN'S CALL on which, before anyone 'fixes' it in the renderer. Measure after: the jetty count should go to zero or become an intended, named thing. RULED (Ben, 2026-10-17): NO - generation should not lay them. Treat a one-sided water crossing as a bug in road generation: lay BOTH halves of a bridge or neither. The jetty count roads.lua prints should go to zero. Note the pass already counts a link as laid only if a crossing was written, so this is a separate hole - find where a route lays its land-to-water half and then fails to lay the water-to-land half, and make the pair atomic. Re-run roads.lua (it prints the deck and single-link counts) and road_generation_harness, and report the road-tile and market-pair-cost deltas, since removing half-crossings moves the laid network. DELIVERED 2026-10-17 (live click: Ben, 'The roads draw right now'). CAUSE: once a crossing could have a water end, both stamps laid every consecutive pair of a route including the water ones - right in the middle of a strait, wrong at the ends, so a route whose first or last cells were water wrote half a bridge from the shore onto water that continued nowhere: laid, counted, billed by upkeep, and drawn as a jetty once decks landed. Attribution over eight seeds: ancient corridor pass 7169, national lattice 4, market joins and trunk 0 - the ancient pass's own comment still claimed stamp_edge skipped water, which stopped being true on 2026-10-17. FIX: a route's terminal water run is the atomic unit, dropped whole, the route laid up to the last shore; an interior run is bounded by land by construction and lays as before. The two-water-tile cap and the no-open-ocean rule are untouched. JETTIES 105 -> 0; roaded water tiles 170 -> 22, shore crossings 160 -> 33, spans 40 -> 6, and no market lost its backbone (off-backbone after the pass 37 -> 37, 0 unexcused). THE TOOL IS SAVED, not left in the Lua script: road_generation_harness carries R7b (no water tile of the shipped field carries exactly one crossing) and R7b' (no road on an uncrossable side), printing the counts and the refusals per pass every run. Verified on main: ROAD GEN AUDIT OK, R7b pooled 448 roaded water tiles with 0 single-crossing, roads 40/0, world_determinism, save_roundtrip.

BL-1378.author: Claude (found delivering BL-1347/1348/1357, 2026-10-18)
BL-1378.title: Two market_viability FULL runs on the same commit disagree about which shards fail
BL-1378.design: SPRINT 55 (found 2026-10-18 reconciling two lanes' reports). On commit 29e5a796 the roads lane reported market_viability FULL as 'no failing row in any shard', pooled G1 92.2 / G1t50 88.6 / G1b 3.0 / G2 182.3 / G3 96.2. The road-rules lane's probe-off run of the same commit reported pooled 91.9 / 89.6 / 3.2 / 187.6 / 96.4 WITH sub-target rows on seeds 11, 40, 12 and 9. A deterministic harness on one commit should give one answer. FIRST SUSPECT, and it is a trap the skill itself documents: market_viability EXITS 0 ON A FAILED GATE, so 'ALL SHARDS EXIT 0' never meant 'no failing row' - the roads lane may have over-read its exit codes. That does not explain the pooled numerators differing, which is the part that matters. CHECK: whether par_seeds' merge recomputes pooled figures from shard numerators as its doc claims, whether a shard can be silently short (a timed-out or requeued shard contributing fewer worlds), and whether the runs used the same tier. If the pooled figures really can drift run to run, every gate reading in the backlog is softer than it looks and that is worth knowing before a sprint close reads one. OBSERVATION 2026-10-18 supporting the hypothesis: a FULL run started from the main session reported "market_viability over 16 seed(s) in 2 shard(s) [full]" where both lanes earlier ran the same tier in 16 shards - the runner sizes its shard set by available cores and another session was sweeping at the time. Shard count should be irrelevant to the verdict (each shard is the unchanged harness handed --seeds), which is exactly why it is the thing to check: if the merge recomputes pooled figures from shard numerators as its doc claims, a shard that contributes fewer worlds than its seed list - timed out, requeued, or short - would move the pooled numerator without failing anything. Compare a 16-shard and a 2-shard run of one commit and diff the per-seed numerators, not just the pooled line. RESOLVED 2026-10-18 by a third run. A FULL sweep from the main session on the merged tree, split into 2 SHARDS where the lanes used 16, reproduced the road-rules lane after figures DIGIT FOR DIGIT: G1 92.0 (1481/1610), G1t50 88.1 (1750/1986), G1b 3.1 (50/1610), G2 182.1 (753527/413706), G3 95.9 (1776/1851), all five gates pass, all shards exit 0, 1270 s wall. So shard count does NOT move the pooled figures and par_seeds merge is sound - the hypothesis is disproved, which is the useful half. WHAT IS LEFT is that one lane measured its before by PROBE-OFF (rules disabled, site pass short-circuited) rather than by building the commit, and a probe-off drifts from the commit wherever disabling code is not the same as code never having been there - which is where the 5.5 points of G2 went. Plus the roads lane almost certainly over-read ALL SHARDS EXIT 0 as no failing row, which this harness does not mean. BOTH LESSONS ARE NOW WRITTEN INTO DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md (A baseline is a commit, not a probe-off), together with the --seeds-is-a-count trap that explained the haulage mismatch, so the next lane does not pay for them again.

BL-1380.author: Claude (found by the BL-1379 lane, confirmed by the main session, 2026-10-18)
BL-1380.title: construction_progress fails 13 assertions since the road gate landed: its fixture places a building on a roadless tile
BL-1380.design: SPRINT 55 (found by the BL-1379 lane, confirmed on main by the main session, 2026-10-18). scripts/verify/construction_progress.lua was 910/0 before BL-1347 and is now 793 pass / 13 FAIL. BL-1381.author: Claude (found by the BL-1380 lane, 2026-10-18)
BL-1381.title: The verify summary calls every failure a golden diff, which has now sent two readers to the wrong conclusion
BL-1381.design: SPRINT 55 (found by the BL-1380 lane, 2026-10-18). verify_api.cpp:7088 prints 'verify: %d capture(s) failed golden diff, %d script error(s)' from m_verify_failures - a counter that totals verify.expect failures AND golden diffs together. CONSEQUENCE, twice over in one day: the delivering lane started from a false premise, and so did I - BL-1380 was filed saying 13 capture goldens diffed and would need Ben's ruling on a re-bless, when construction_progress.lua has NO goldens whatsoever (all 28 of its captures log 'no golden ... (capture-only)'). DELIVERED 2026-10-18: m_verify_golden_failures counts the image diffs alone (app_capture.cpp's two sites), and both the per-script line and the run summary now name the two kinds apart - 'N failure(s): G golden diff(s), A assertion(s)'. BL-1387.author: Claude (found smoke-testing BL-1386, 2026-10-19)
BL-1387.title: scripts/verify/roads_painted.lua crashes the app at its last framing, and does so on main
BL-1387.design: SPRINT 55 (found smoke-testing BL-1386, 2026-10-19). `ProjectIo --verify scripts/verify/roads_painted.lua` dies with 'fatal hardware exception 0xC0000005 (access violation)' immediately after the capture `roads_painted_lane_port_rung3` - i.e. while baking or painting the LANE_PORT framing's last rung. PROVEN PRE-EXISTING, not BL-1386's: the same crash, at the same address, with every one of that item's renderer changes reverted to HEAD and rebuilt (the check was run three ways - with the change, with its bake half switched off, and on the committed files). The ground disk cache was EMPTY at the time, so it is not a stale-cache read. CONSEQUENCE: one of the committed road checks cannot be run at all, which is how a renderer regression gets through - every other road check passes, so a green sweep reads as cover it does not give. THE WORK: get a stack (a Debug build under a debugger, or an address-sanitised run), name the pass that faults - the suspicion is the lane/deck geometry at the widest rung, since the crash follows a sea-lane port framing - and fix it. Do not 'fix' it by trimming the script's last framing: the framing is the check. DELIVERED 2026-10-19 (Ben ruled: bound the blit, keep the check on the software renderer). THE CAUSE, read off a symbolised trace rather than guessed: a ground image is drawn at whatever scale the camera asks for, so at the closest rung a page is described as a destination rectangle MEASURED AT 50,025 x 20,254 px against a view of 1,941 x 1,281 - twenty-five times the window across, the rest off screen (the first write of this said 'hundreds of thousands', which was inferred; the number above is logged). ImGui records that quad, and SDL's SOFTWARE renderer - the one --verify forces so goldens stay machine-independent - turns an axis-aligned textured quad into a scaled blit whose fixed-point source step is computed from the DESTINATION extent; at those extents it walks off the source surface and dies in Blit8888to8888PixelAlphaSwizzleAVX2 (SDL_blit_A.c:1114), reached through SDL_BlitSurface and SW_RunCommandQueue from SDL_RenderPresent. The renderer's own clip rectangle hides the overflow's RESULT but does not stop SDL computing the blit from the unclipped extent first. THE FIX: draw_ground_rect clips the quad to the view and moves its UVs by the same fraction, so the part that was never drawn is no longer described - no pixel changes, and the previously fatal capture renders correctly. TWO WRONG GUESSES CAME FIRST (a texture-upload length check, a draw-list index split); both were reverted or kept on their own merits, and the lesson is the one the item now carries: get the stack before the fix. The crash report was taught to name the module, the faulting function, the file and line, and what an access violation touched - that is what turned a four-hour bisect into one run. VERIFIED on the software renderer: roads_painted 0 failures (it had been dying at its last framing), roads 0, throughput_lens 0, ground_bake still exactly its nine pre-existing BL-1388 rows and no others. WHOSE DEFECT: SDL accepts the rectangle, documents no limit on it, and then mis-samples it - over fifty thousand destination columns its fixed-point source accumulator lands one sample past the source surface - so the rounding is SDL's, reproduced on the pinned release-3.2.0, and the hardware renderer draws the same quad correctly. The clip is therefore a WORKAROUND for someone else's arithmetic as well as the right thing on its own terms, and it is deliberately narrow: it clips to the view and nothing else, does nothing once SDL samples a wide blit correctly, and never shrinks what a capture shows (the UVs move by exactly the fraction the edges did). Ben's ruling to keep the check on software stands on verifier-visual's own rule that goldens must be renderer-independent.

BL-1390.author: Ben (in play, 2026-10-19)
BL-1390.title: A crossing whose halves differ in tier rendered at one tier
BL-1390.design: SPRINT 55. BEN, in play 2026-10-19: "when one half of a road is one tier, and the other half is another tier, only one road tier gets rendered. We should make sure that each half of that tile's road gets rendered as the correct road tier." CAUSE: a road is an EDGE and each edge carries its own tier, but both renderers weighted the whole TILE by max_road_tier - the bake took one tier a piece, the canvas one colour and width a cell - so a tile with a Track one way and a Highway the other drew both halves as Highway. MEASURED before the fix: 845 tiles of the shipped 1960 start carry two tiers across 2629 crossings, about one roaded tile in six, before a player builds anything. DELIVERED 2026-10-19 at 654a6a8e: the seam already existed (the canvas curve split at its apex so each half could take its own edge's FOG, and a baked curve recorded the arclength where its halves meet), so the tier rides both - per-direction colour and width on the canvas with the apex capped by the heavier half, route_piece::tier_b for the half past the split, tile_pieces reading each crossing's tier off the edge mask, and the painter resolving which half a pixel is on before taking a width (culling at the wider of the two so the heavy half is never clipped). Rail and sea lanes are TILE fields and keep one tier. PROOF: route_link_audit gained mixed_tier_tiles and two_tier_pieces - 603 of 6831 baked runs now taper at the apex, where the count was 0 by construction before. roads.lua and throughput_lens green; the two red checks found while smoke-testing are BL-1387 and BL-1388, both proven pre-existing. ID MOVED on integration, 2026-10-19: this item was filed as BL-1386 in sprint 55's session while sprint 56's worktree filed a DIFFERENT BL-1386 (NO_REALM_CLOSES_EMPTY) at the same time - the collision next_id.js cannot see across an unmerged branch. Sprint 56's keeps BL-1386 because its id is cited in nine source files and its sprint ruling register; this one moved to BL-1390 and its three citations (route_paint.hpp, route_paint.cpp, body_surface_canvas.cpp, verify_api.cpp) moved with it. The commits that landed it (654a6a8e, 696753f1) still say BL-1386, which is history and stays.

BL-1395.author: Ben (2026-10-21, NR-1059); filed by Claude
BL-1395.title: Rival siting prices and lays the whole hub chain a build needs to reach its capital
BL-1395.design: GRANTED (Ben, 2026-10-21, NR-1059), recorded in AI_OPPONENT.md section 11 'AI lays a hub chain to reach the capital'. Since BL-1356 a hub delivers only when it chains back to its nation's capital (LOGISTICS.md section How a tile's points get to it), so corp_ai's source_capex (corp_ai.cpp ~1247) prices an out-of-reach build at ONE hub and the build path (~3311) places that hub on or beside the site - on far ground it costs upkeep and covers nothing, and under NR-1057 it adds nothing to the pool either. THE WORK: price the build at the whole chain lp_route_to would need (the same outward rule generation's seed_logistics_sources step 1 lays: a hub that carries the site at full strength and touches the chain, else a hub on the chain's edge nearest the site, repeated), and lay it in the SAME decision. TERMS (the grant): one decision, priced and laid in the tick the build is chosen, nothing carried to a later tick, a chain the scorer cannot afford that tick is not started; never for the player's nation or champion; only on ground the builder may build on. Pure, seeded, deterministic, replayable, legal verbs only, never a planner. Reuse generation's chain-laying rather than a second copy of it. MEASURE: market_viability FULL (G1, G3 - rivals stop wasting hubs) and rival hub counts against the BL-1356 landing. DELIVERED 2026-10-21. lp_plan_chain (logistic_points) plans the chain without placing it - the rule generation lays by; generation itself keeps its committed loop, byte-identical (census seeds 0/28/46: 216 hubs, 17 ports, unchanged). corp_ai prices a build at the whole planned chain, every hub tile passing the build verb's own door (construct_for: logistics reach 24 from COMPLETED anchors, era and placement gates, never the build's own tile), so a chain the door will not admit this tick plans as unreachable and the site is skipped (traced as no_chain) rather than half-laid; after the build it lays the chain hub by hub, re-planned from the world as it stands, stopping once covered and never beyond the hubs it was priced with. On the PLAYER's nation's ground the 2026-10-15 rule stands exactly - one hub on or beside the site - pending NR-1060. COLD REVIEW: found plans with door-refused tiles, a generation drift, over-laying, the player-ground reading, an untraced skip and thin evidence; all fixed or raised. EVIDENCE: corp_ai_harness chain scene - a rival builds a mine 20 tiles out and lays exactly 2 hubs in the same decision, the mine covered once they stand, each hub needed; under a 4-tile door the site is never built and no hub laid, across six evaluations. market_viability FULL before (BL-1356) -> after: G1 94.7 -> 94.6, G1t50 86.8 -> 89.3, G1b 2.3 -> 2.4, G2 170.5 -> 170.3, G3 94.9 -> 95.9; per seed G1t50 only seed 46 under 85 (84.4; seed 28 77.1 -> 87.6). haulage --far-trade unchanged (900 / 959 convoys). logistic_points_harness 84/0, corp_ai_harness ALL PASS, decision_trace / ai_trade / corp_ai_predictive pass, world_determinism ALL PASS, save_roundtrip OK.

BL-1396.author: Ben (2026-10-21); filed by Claude
BL-1396.title: A port's points reach full strength across 50 water tiles, fading to zero at 100
BL-1396.design: Ben, 2026-10-21, during BL-1395: 'we can extend logistics points over water, let's say a port stretches 50 tiles'; RULED the same message: full strength to 50, gone at 100 (the road's double-distance fade), and built after BL-1395. DESIGNED: LOGISTICS.md section One pool, 'A port stretches fifty tiles over water'. THE CHANGE: lp_full_reach[sea] 12 -> 50 and lp_fade_length[sea] 8 -> 50. Distances are network cost: a water step costs 1, a land step lp_offnet_step (3), so 50 water tiles is 50 cost - check whether 'tiles' should also be read across the landing step. CONSEQUENCES TO MEASURE: generation's sea bridge (BL-1356) reaches far wider seas, so fewer ports and far fewer stranded consumers; a port's field now spans a large area, so watch per-source flood cost in the resolver and the census seed_ms; the Throughput lens and hover card read lp_full_reach directly. Measure lp_coverage_census, market_viability FULL and haulage_measure --far-trade before and after; budget a cold review. DELIVERED 2026-10-22. Ben's rulings (LOGISTICS.md section One pool): 50 full / 100 gone; OVER WATER ONLY - a port's points cross water and land on the shore, no further inland; LAKES TOO (NR-1061 resolved) though a port still stands only on a sea coast. lp_sea_walk is the one sea field: all six hex sides (a legal port with sea only on a diagonal side reached nothing under a 4-way walk - cold review), a landing ends the walk, every step 1; lp_distance_field's sea branch and generation's bridge both call it. A port's field is cached in world::lp_sea_fields by port tile (a sea field reads only which tiles are water), cleared with the logistics caches and on load. Large enclosed bodies at or over the lake size cap are already SEA (TILES.md), so inland seas take ports. MEASURED before (BL-1395) -> after: market_viability FULL G1 94.6 -> 95.1, G1t50 89.3 -> 90.3, G1b 2.4 -> 2.5, G2 170.3 -> 176.9, G3 95.9 -> 95.5, all pass; per seed G1t50 under 85 on 12 (83.8) and 9 (81.0); haulage window E 900 -> 868 convoys (7554.4 -> 7493.2 u), window Y 959 -> 909 (5920.6 -> 7179.9 u); census 0/28/46 every consumer covered, 217 hubs; seeding 178 -> 565 ms over three seeds (the bridge's wider sea search). logistic_points_harness 93/0, lp_pool_harness M/L1/L2/L5 pass, corp_ai / decision_trace / corp_ai_predictive pass, world_determinism ALL PASS, save_roundtrip OK.

BL-1398.author: Ben (2026-10-22/23); filed by Claude
BL-1398.title: No capital starts dark: the firms on a nation's ground fund its opening node bill, and the gate pays network nodes first
BL-1398.design: Ben, 2026-10-22/23, during BL-1367 (capital-first seeding). Every capital now holds a Logistic Point source, a minor's as a major's, so every nation holding network nodes carries a bill for them from the first tick, and a nation with an empty chest idles its capital's hub at the funding gate. RULED: 'No capital starts dark' (NATION_GENERATION.md section Pass 7). Option 2 (extend 'no realm closes the history empty' by raising the endowment floor) was SWEPT AND REJECTED: treasury_census over the 16 library seeds, floor 500 / 750 / 1000 (the cap) / 2000 / 5000 (cap lifted for the measure only): nations short of a year of their state bill 55 / 51 / 41 / 31 / 21, capitals dark at the handoff 44 / 33 / 33 / 28 / 18, seeds with the median outside 1,000-2,000 4 / 5 / 7 / 16 / 16; the 18 left at 5000 are exactly the nations the history never held, which no floor reaches. Ben: keep the floor at 500 and fund by option 1. BUILT: fund_state_nodes_from_firms (state_industry.cpp), at the fold after the founding reserve and before the reading at the gate (finish_campaign_world, mirrored in harness_params and lp_coverage_census): a nation whose chest is under k_state_founding_reserve_ticks (16) of its network nodes' share of the state bill is topped up to it by the corporations holding buildings on its ground, each by its building share and never above its balance, the remainder asked again of the others; a transfer, never a mint (counted, 0). Every firm alike, the player's future seat included (Ben, 2026-10-23). AND THE GATE PAYS NETWORK NODES FIRST (Ben, 2026-10-23; NATIONS.md section State industry): gate_walk_buildings walks hubs, stations and ports before every other state building, so a nation short of money idles its plants before its hubs - every tick of play, not only the opening. Cold review (two rounds) fixed: the top-up buying a plant ahead of the hub (the gate order), the trigger keyed to the node bill, a mint counter. MEASURED (16 seeds, floor 500): coverage census at the fold, 78 nations short of the node bill, 36 funded (19,414 credits moved), 2 still short, 42 with no firm on their ground, 0 minted; 21 capitals dark at the fold and their consumers 0, every rule passing; treasury_census at the handoff, 37 capitals dark (20 of them never held by the history), majors short of a year 4, medians outside the band on 3 seeds (4 before). market_viability FULL pooled G1 95.7, G1t50 89.1, G1b 2.6, G2 157.5, G3 96.4, all pass; haulage --far-trade window E 834 convoys (7062.1 u), window Y 971 (7612.3 u). world_determinism ALL PASS, save_roundtrip OK, no_empty_chest_harness, corp_ai, ai_trade, decision_trace pass; lp_pool, state_industry, railway and nation_budget_harness reds unchanged from before.

That worked while the tile RECORD was version-independent. BL-1340 (v53) made it version-dependent - r_tile_v reads a u16 road_edges at the current version and a u8 legacy road_level below it - so a v53 body of bytes labelled v49 desyncs at the first tile and the reader refuses the whole stream. The assertion is therefore failing for a true reason: that stream is not a v49 stream. THE FIX is to produce a REAL old stream the way BL-1340 already does for its own case - world_save.cpp has write_world_snapshot_pre_road_edges / write_world_snapshot_at for exactly this - rather than relabelling bytes, and NOT to relax the row. BL-1392.author: Claude (found verifying BL-1370/1371, 2026-10-17)
BL-1392.title: construction_ledger_tabs dies in staging: its fixture is refused for want of a road, not for want of funds
BL-1392.design: SPRINT 55 (found verifying BL-1370/1371 on main, 2026-10-17). scripts/verify/construction_ledger_tabs.lua exits 1 with ZERO assertions run - it dies in base.stage_ui_fixture (lib.lua:340, raised at :223) with 'fixture could not place a military base near the player's works: insufficient_funds'.
